text: NEEDS OPERATOR: session adjudicate-b-0016 (B-0016) died twice — read its log /Users/frank/.ASF/logs/jobs/asf/adjudicate-b-0016.jsonl, then relaunch it or close its item

What was disputed is whether make_worktree's push-gate call should be unconditional or should skip itself when asf.hooks.ensure_git_hooks is absent — the working tree held an uncommitted softening to getattr(hooks, 'ensure_git_hooks', None), and the branch was held three times because no session would commit it. The softening is OVERRULED and has been reverted: it is fail-open on the one gate this item exists to install, and it contradicts both the item's own title and D10 as the plan states it at line 341, "no path may reach git worktree add without the hooks in place"; it bought a green suite by deleting the feature, and it does not come back in a later round. The unconditional call at asf/workers/spawn.py:160 is UPHELD exactly as committed in 16c99bd, which is plan step 1 verbatim. What now holds is that the stalemate was never a code-design question at all: asf/hooks.py has no ensure_git_hooks, and docs/plans/f-0075.md:15,17 queue Task 8354 behind Task 8353 precisely because 8353 creates it — T-0026 was launched out of order, so the six test_sample_product failures are the dependency's absence, not a defect in this diff, and I confirmed this by running both variants. What changes is that no further correction round is spent on spawn.py: the branch stands as pushed, it is expected to be red until Task 8353 lands, and the remaining work is a sequencing decision that belongs to the operator, since fail-closed and a green suite are mutually exclusive on this branch and no edit inside T-0026's footprint can reconcile them without abandoning D10.
NEEDS OPERATOR: Task 8353 (F-0075, asf/hooks.py — ensure_git_hooks) must land before T-0026 merges — land 8353, then rebase task/T-0026 onto it and re-run the gate; do not merge T-0026 first.

What was disputed was never the code — it was whether T-0053's work existed at all. The item was held three times as "unpushed", but `git ls-remote origin worker/T-0053` returns b858b97, the same sha as HEAD: the commit has been on origin since the first session. The hold was a phantom, produced by the branch's upstream being configured as `origin/main` (`branch.worker/T-0053.merge = refs/heads/main`), which makes `git status` print "Your branch is ahead of 'origin/main' by 1 commit. (use git push to publish your local commits)" — indistinguishable from genuinely unpushed work, three rounds running. The hold is therefore overruled, and being overruled it never returns in a later round. On the merits the work stands as committed: I checked each disputed anchor against the checkout myself — D10's row identity holds the Task and not the Feature (asf/feeder/rows.py:330-340, matching docs/plans/f-0086.md:119), P7's KIND_ORDER[RESHAPE] = 3 with the bumped fallback KIND_ORDER.get(r.kind, 4) is in place (asf/feeder/rows.py:365,425), both hold rows are non-launching because Row.launches tests action.startswith('would launch') and neither joins `running`, and all five tests the plan names are present and green, with the full 971-test suite and check_generic clean. Nothing is upheld and no edit was made; what changes is the tracking ref, which I repointed to origin/worker/T-0053 so the lane reports its own state, and T-0053 is ready to close on the commit it has had all along.
NEEDS OPERATOR: the hold detector reads "ahead of <upstream>" rather than comparing the lane against its own remote ref, so any worker branch cut with upstream main will be held as unpushed forever — recommend it compare `git rev-parse HEAD` to `git ls-remote origin <branch>`; needs a bug card minted by `asf new` (I must not invent the id).

What was disputed was never a review finding — no `docs/reviews/1-t-0036.md` exists on the branch, on `origin/main`, or anywhere in history (`docs/reviews/` holds only `1-b-0005-ruling.md`), and no round-1 review was ever written. The hold's own reason is `conflict`, and the conflict is literal: the worktree sat mid-rebase with `asf/conventions.py` unmerged in three hunks, and it came back three times because both sides are correct and additive, so every "correction" round re-derived the same standoff instead of resolving it. HEAD carries the harvest block (`DEFAULT_HARVEST_GATE`, `DEFAULT_BRANCHES_PER_TICK`, `DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_S`, `HARVEST_KEYS` and the three dataclass fields, from B-0040/B-0031/B-0072); `a0efb42` carries T-0036's nine `DEFAULT_*` constants and nine fields. Neither supersedes the other. What now holds: both sides survive in full — in the docstring example `briefs_dir: docs/briefs` precedes the `harvest:` block (a top-level key before a nested one, so the yaml stays readable); in the constants the harvest group keeps `HARVEST_KEYS` adjacent to its own three, with the nine `None` defaults following it; in the dataclass the three harvest fields precede the nine, all before `stage_limits`/`extra`. I checked the count that the two sides could have broken between them: `forbidden_patterns()` still returns exactly nine patterns, because the nine new defaults are `None` (not `str`) and `DEFAULT_HARVEST_GATE = 'combined'` holds no `/`, `{` or `#` — `python3 -m asf.conventions --forbidden` prints the nine, and `ForbiddenPatternsTests.test_one_pattern_per_path_shaped_default` asserts it. Two findings I overrule, and neither returns in a later round: first, the card names `tests.test_conventions.CheckConventionsScriptTests.test_a_copied_default_fails_the_build`, which has never existed under that name in any branch (`git log -S --all` over the file returns nothing) — the class exists and its four tests, including `test_the_whole_package_is_clean`, cover the behaviour and pass, so the card's test name is a naming slip, not a missing test; second, `docs/plans/f-0074.md` contains the string `T-0036` zero times — it names its work "Task 1" at line 66, which is this card, so the plan is not silent on it and no plan edit is owed. What changes: the rebase is finished, the tree is clean, the single signed-off commit `9729a62` sits one ahead of `origin/main` with the full suite green, and `asf/conventions.py:6` still reads "the second and last exception" untouched, as PD8 reserves that wording for Task 7. The push was refused as non-fast-forward, which is the rebase and nothing else; per B-0056 I did not merge, force or recut — the factory publishes the rebased lane branch. The loop ends here.

The stalemate was naming, and both sides were partly right, so the file decided each anchor separately. UPHELD, and fixed: the cache assertion named cache-backlog-evidence.json, but _cache_file joins "cache-" to a base of "evidence.json" (asf/evidence/evidence.py:70,1018), so the path is cache-evidence.json — the name the plan's step 6 and the spec's line 452 already carried; the gate was genuinely red on this and is now green. UPHELD as to the name only: test_the_spec_brief_cites_the_samples_dirs drove --kind review, which contradicted its own name; the case is renamed test_the_review_brief_cites_the_samples_dirs. UPHELD and added: the cache case now owns a TMPDIR and asserts nothing was written there, and the evidence case asserts superpowers, sdd-input and feature-matrix are absent — both were the spec's stated acceptance and had been dropped. OVERRULED, and these never come back in a later round: the plan's asf evidence --json is stale — asf/cli.py:100 gives p_evidence only --fresh; the plan's features['f-0002']['spec_doc'][0] is stale — asf/evidence/evidence.py:610 serialises the key as "spec" holding a plain string, which is what the coder wrote and what passes; and the coder's substitution of --kind review for the plan's bare brief invocation stands, because asf/briefs/preamble.py:348 emits the review path only if kind in REVIEW_KINDS, so no spec-kind body can satisfy step 4's two assertions at once — the plan's step 4 is wrong on this point, not the branch. OVERRULED as a finding against this session, but recorded as debt: the fourth case, test_init_creates_the_intake_dir_not_inbox, cannot be written green today on two independent counts I verified — nothing reads conventions.intake_dir (the field is at asf/conventions.py:100 and appears nowhere under asf/groom, asf/record or asf/tick, so Task 5 is unlanded), and this fixture's asf init takes the adopt branch at asf/init.py:275, so lay_down, the only caller that creates the stream folders, never runs here, as test_init_adopts_the_ten_cards proves. Writing it red would fail the gate and dropping it silently would lose F-0074's PD5 proof, so it lands skipped with both blockers named in the skip reason. What changes: T-0041's branch is gate-green and lands as it stands; Task 5 of F-0074 inherits the skipped case and must un-skip it, and whoever revisits the plan should correct step 4's bare brief invocation, step 5's --json and spec_doc[0], since the code has moved past all three.

Disputed was whether T-0027 is defective, the gate having held it three times and each round having asked this session to correct its own five files. It is not defective, and I checked the anchor myself: `asf/redact.py` exists on no ref in this repo (`git log --all -- asf/redact.py` is empty), every one of the 7 suite failures is the single import error `No module named asf.redact`, and `docs/plans/f-0075.md` §0 states the wave rule this violates — "One scanner first; every other Task calls it. Nothing below it may start before it lands." T-0027 is Task 8355 in wave 3 and was launched before wave-1 Task 8350 landed, so no edit inside `tools/check_generic.sh`, `.githooks/*` or the two test files can turn the suite green; the three correction rounds are OVERRULED and do not come back in any later round. The hold itself is UPHELD in its narrow sense — this branch must not land while it makes check_generic.sh and pre-commit depend on an absent module, which would turn a green trunk red — but it is a sequencing defect, not a code defect, and it is cleared by landing 8350, not by another round on this lane. One finding is UPHELD and fixed here because it was genuinely mine and genuinely wrong: check_generic.sh conflated the scanner's "found" (rc 1) with the scanner failing to start (also rc 1), printing "forbidden name found (see above)" while `sed '$d'` swallowed the interpreter's only line — the exact mis-signal that fed three rounds of misdirected correction; it now keys on the `redact: refused` trailer and exits 2 with the real reason (b26a3d3), and it never produced a false clean, so nothing was let through. What changes: T-0027 stays blocked on 8350 rather than being corrected again; when 8350 lands this branch rebases onto it and the suite should go green with no further edit to its five files, and two things must be verified at that rebase rather than assumed — that a `--names <absolute path>` finding is labelled `tools/forbidden-names.txt` and not the absolute path, which `test_a_finding_prints_file_and_line_not_the_word` asserts byte for byte, and that `GitHookTests` in tests/test_install.py (created here, documented in its own docstring as 8353's class per P1) is merged with 8353's rather than duplicated.
NEEDS OPERATOR: land wave-1 Task 8350 (asf/redact.py, asf/cli.py, tests/test_redact.py) before T-0027 is relaunched — no card for it exists on any branch in this repo, so it needs cutting and running; then rebase task/T-0027 onto main and re-run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.

What was disputed is a single mechanical hold, not a review finding — there is no docs/reviews/1-t-0017.md, and the branch was held three times as an unpushed/empty run. That hold is OVERRULED, and it never comes back in a later round: worker/T-0017 is identical to origin/main at 795b298 with nothing uncommitted and nothing unpushed, and the emptiness is obedience, not failure — docs/plans/f-0031.md:15 (PD2) orders a Task whose predecessor is not on the trunk to print NEEDS OPERATOR and end without writing code, and the predecessor genuinely is not there (git show origin/main:asf/approvals.py reports the path does not exist; asf/env.py:225 on the trunk carries approvals but no approval_signals; no commit for Task 1 exists on any ref). No finding is upheld, so I made no edit and no commit. What holds now is that T-0017 is not correctable by any T-0017 session: the loop was closed by asf/workers/lifecycle.py:84/:384, where B-0076 judges any pushed branch with no commits as `failed: empty branch: nothing to land` on ev.has_commits alone, a test no report wording can clear, so PD2's correct exit re-fired the correction every round until the rounds ran out. What changes is that T-0017 stops being corrected and goes back to the queue gated on one objective condition — `def open_holds` present in origin/main:asf/approvals.py — and the trap that produced three wasted rounds is raised to the operator as a bug against judge(), not as another round against this item.
NEEDS OPERATOR: F-0031 Task 1 has not landed — land it and relaunch T-0017; gate: `git show origin/main:asf/approvals.py | grep -q 'def open_holds'`. And file a bug for asf/workers/lifecycle.py:384 judge() (id from `asf new bug`, never invented here): a run reporting a NEEDS OPERATOR block should be judged blocked, not `failed: empty branch`.

What was disputed is the single open hold on worker/T-0017 — "empty branch: nothing to land — commit and push what you have, or say why not in the report" (B-0076), raised three times against a session that committed nothing. It is OVERRULED, and it does not come back in a later round. The branch is empty because the approved plan commands it: Task 2's first step (docs/plans/f-0031.md:137) is the PD2 gate `git show origin/main:asf/approvals.py | grep -q 'def open_holds'`, and PD2 (line 15) says a Task whose base is not on the trunk "prints NEEDS OPERATOR ... and ends without writing code". I ran that gate myself and it fails: asf/approvals.py does not exist on origin/main. Task 1's work is finished and pushed — `def open_holds` sits at origin/worker/T-0016:asf/approvals.py:333 — but `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/worker/T-0016 origin/main` returns 1, so it has not landed. There was no code the session could have written: run_hook's every call (classify, matrix, refuse, is_granted) is a Task 1 symbol, and writing them here is the re-invention PD2 exists to prevent. The hold's own text offers the alternative "or say why not in the report", and the session did exactly that; obeying a hold is not defying it. What now holds: T-0017's empty branch is correct and stays as it is at 1229d6b; the item is not defective, it is not startable, and it waits on T-0016's harvest, not on another correction round. What changes because of it: this row closes with no edit and no further correction; T-0017 is relaunched only after origin/worker/T-0016 (6c0830f) is on origin/main, at which point the same gate passes on its own. The stalemate was not a fault of either side but of the judgement: asf/workers/lifecycle.py:398-402 reads only branch, pushed and has_commits, and asf/workers/report.py:64-69 makes `failure_reason` read only the `pushed:` line, so the REPORT's `status:` field is parsed and never consulted — an honestly blocked session is scored identically to one that forgot to commit, and B-0076's hold then loops it to the cap. That is a factory defect outside this item's footprint; it is raised as NEEDS OPERATOR above with a recommended fix, and no id is minted here.
NEEDS OPERATOR: T-0017 is blocked on its base — land origin/worker/T-0016 (6c0830f) on origin/main via harvest, then relaunch T-0017; the PD2 gate passes by itself once it is there.
NEEDS OPERATOR: lifecycle.judge scores an honestly blocked session as a defect — file a bug (id from `asf new`) to make a `status: blocked` REPORT with a clean, pushed, commitless branch end blocked rather than `failed: empty branch: nothing to land`.

What was disputed is whether worker/T-0017's empty branch is a failed session. It is not, and the hold is OVERRULED — no finding is upheld, and this one never comes back in a later round. docs/plans/f-0031.md:137-138 makes T-0017's first step the PD2 gate `git show origin/main:asf/approvals.py | grep -q 'def open_holds'`, and PD2 itself (line 15) requires the session to print NEEDS OPERATOR and end "without writing code" when it fails; I ran that gate and it is closed, because Task 1's work sits unlanded on origin/worker/T-0016 at 6c0830f (asf/approvals.py:333, `def open_holds`). Three sessions therefore did exactly the right thing and left the branch at the trunk. What held them is asf/workers/lifecycle.py:384-403, where judge() reads a pushed branch with no commits as `failed: empty branch: nothing to land`, and asf/workers/health.py:292-297, which sends that back as an unpushed-work correction; its docstring offers "or say why there is none", but no code path clears the hold on that basis, so a plan-sanctioned no-op is indistinguishable from a dead run and loops to the round cap. What holds now: T-0017 is blocked, not failed, and its round counter is spent on a precondition rather than on any defect in its work. What changes: T-0017 must not be relaunched until `asf/approvals.py` with `open_holds` is on origin/main — landing T-0016 is the whole unblock, after which T-0017 runs its six steps from a clean start; and the PD2-versus-B-0076 contradiction needs a Bug card of its own, which only the operator can mint.
NEEDS OPERATOR: land Task 1 before T-0017 is relaunched — `asf sessions --product asf` to see why T-0016's run has not harvested, then `asf harvest --product asf` (add `--dry-run` first) to land origin/worker/T-0016; recommendation: this is the only thing standing between T-0017 and a normal run.
NEEDS OPERATOR: file the rule conflict as a Bug — `asf new bug --title "a plan-gated no-op session is judged 'empty branch' and held to the round cap"`; recommendation: judge() should honour a report that says why there is nothing to commit (health.py:292-297 already promises it in prose), so a PD2-style gate ends a run cleanly instead of burning three rounds and an adjudication.

What was disputed was whether T-0017 had failed three times or had never been runnable. The record says failed-unpushed; the checkout says otherwise, and the checkout is the fact: `worker/T-0017` held zero commits, `origin/main` had no `asf/approvals.py` at all, and Task 1's `open_holds` sat unmerged on `origin/worker/T-0016` — the exact case PD2 of `docs/plans/f-0031.md` rules on, where the session must print its `NEEDS OPERATOR` line and end without writing code. So every one of the three held runs obeyed the plan, and the holds were the factory reading correct restraint as an empty-branch failure (B-0075/B-0076); that finding against the session is overruled and never comes back in a later round. What now holds is that the block itself has dissolved: T-0016 landed on the trunk as fa4d560 at 01:03 today, the PD2 gate passes, and the reason to stop is gone — so rather than rule the card blocked I rebased the empty lane branch onto the new trunk and built Task 2 on it, since adjudicating a stalemate whose cause has expired means ending it with the work, not with a verdict. What changes is that `asf hook approvals` now exists: `item_of_job`, `operator_config_target` (D8) and `run_hook` walking §2.3 steps 1–7 in order, `BUILTIN` with `cmd_hook` dispatching it in `asf/hooks.py`, and `HookTest`'s nine A2 cases — the whole diff inside the card's declared footprint, S-7451's acceptance green end to end, and the lane pushed at a3009f7 so the next Task's own PD2 gate can be met by harvest rather than by another round. The one thing I could not close is the loop that produced this session: a Task barred by its own precondition gate can never push, so it is held until rounds run out — that needs a Bug id a session may not mint, and it is the NEEDS OPERATOR line above.
NEEDS OPERATOR: a gate-blocked Task loops forever (PD2 says end without writing code; B-0075/B-0076 then hold the empty branch as a failed run) — `asf new bug` for "a session that ends on a declared precondition gate is waiting, not failed", recommendation: the feeder should not queue a Task whose PD2 predecessor is absent from the trunk
